new_entries.name: Mechanical feedback liquidation
causal_chain: A large share of market participants run pre-programmed, rule-based selling strategies (e.g. portfolio insurance) that mechanically sell into price declines
An initial price drop triggers these rules to sell, regardless of fundamentals
That selling pushes prices lower, which triggers the same rules to sell again -- a self-reinforcing downdraft
Sell orders vastly outnumber willing buyers near prior prices; liquidity evaporates and the decline accelerates within hours
The vacuum clears only when a liquidity backstop appears or mechanical selling is exhausted

historical_instances.case: https://www.federalreservehistory.org/essays/stock-market-crash-of-1987 -- Black Monday, 19 Oct 1987: the DJIA fell 22.6% in a single session (the largest one-day decline in history); portfolio-insurance selling accelerated the crash as initial losses triggered further rounds of automated selling (Shiller 1988)
historical_instances.source: https://www.federalreservehistory.org/essays/stock-market-crash-of-1987 -- Bernhardt & Eckblad, 'Stock Market Crash of 1987', Federal Reserve History

new_entries.name: Crowded-trade deleveraging
causal_chain: Many highly-leveraged players crowd into similar convergence/relative-value positions, often financed by the same set of counterparties
A shock moves those positions against everyone simultaneously
Margin calls force multiple players to unwind the same trades at once, into a market with no offsetting buyers
Prices gap further against the crowded position, amplifying losses and threatening the leveraged counterparties themselves
A disorderly failure is avoided only by a coordinated recapitalization or backstop that halts the forced simultaneous unwind

historical_instances.case: PENDING-MAC-VERIFICATION -- Long-Term Capital Management, Sept 1998: a hedge fund with ~$4.6B capital but notional derivatives exposure in the trillions saw crowded relative-value trades move against it after the Russian default; the NY Fed convened 14 creditor banks to fund an orderly ~$3.6B recapitalization
historical_instances.source: https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/276/hedgefund.pdf -- President's Working Group on Financial Markets, 'Hedge Funds, Leverage, and the Lessons of Long-Term Capital Management' (1999) [sandbox fetch of the primary Fed speech returned empty; URL routed to citation_check.sh for Mac verification]

instance.case: PENDING-MAC-VERIFICATION -- Japan's asset-price bubble, late 1980s: equity and urban land valuations detached from fundamentals through a self-reinforcing collateral-and-credit loop; the Nikkei peaked end-1989 (~38,900) and land values collapsed through the early 1990s into a prolonged stagnation
instance.source: https://www.imf.org/external/pubs/ft/wp/2009/wp09241.pdf -- Syed, Kang & Tokuoka, 'Lost Decade in Translation', IMF WP/09/241 (2009) [sandbox returned HTTP 200 application/pdf but oversized to display; URL routed to citation_check.sh]

instance.case: https://www.federalreservehistory.org/essays/asian-financial-crisis -- Asian financial crisis, 1997: after Thailand's July 1997 baht devaluation, foreign creditors pulled back across East Asian economies seen as sharing similar vulnerabilities, spreading a depreciation-recession-banking spiral region-wide (Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, South Korea)
instance.source: https://www.federalreservehistory.org/essays/asian-financial-crisis -- Carson & Clark, 'Asian Financial Crisis', Federal Reserve History
